brief: A herb planter of three cells side by side, each with a bin that drains.

requirements.requirement: Herb planter of three cells side by side
requirements.evidence: Three full-depth base pieces in a straight row at axial cells (-1,0), (0,0), (1,0) on level 0, with capOpenFaces and lockJoints applied; check_build reports no issues and meshClash clear.

requirements.requirement: Each cell has a bin that drains
requirements.evidence: bin:-1,0,0, bin:0,0,0 and bin:1,0,0, each the 'Bin, full depth, drained' (hex-bin-full-drain) tray, one per cell. Drainage is as the part's name states; the configurator does not check that the holes actually drain water.
Soil filled in each bin; basil-young in the west cell, parsley-young in the centre, chives-young in the east cell.

requirements.requirement: Material suitability for wet use (waterproofing, food safety, UV/heat resistance)
requirements.evidence: The configurator checks fit and collisions only; material choice for the printed plastic is the user's and was not verified.

finish.summary: Built a three-cell herb planter: three full-depth bases in a row, each holding a drained bin with soil and a young herb (basil, parsley, chives), capped and joint-locked. The configurator reports no rule issues and a clear mesh check. I could not verify the drainage holes or the material's suitability for wet conditions beyond the part names.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
